item.title: Creating art for US coins is tricky. These Pa. artists have made a career of it.
item.description: PHILADELPHIA — If you’ve got coins in your pocket, purse, or wallet, you’re likely carrying around Pennsylvania-created art. The U.S. Mint produces coins in four cities: Denver, Philadelphia, San Francisco, and West Point, New York. But the Philly location — located just a few blocks north of Independence Hall — is the Mint’s hub for engraving, and employs a team of medallic artists who sculpt all the new designs for circulating coins, Congressional medals, and collectible pieces. Yes, sculpts.
